app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured type-specific image and attachment limits, incorrectly rejecting valid uploads or allowing uploads that will fail; the 413 handler at line 246 also reports the wrong limit

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL uploads are unconditionally capped at 10 MB instead of `max_image_size_kb`, preventing sites configured for larger images from importing otherwise-valid image URLs

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL uploads are unconditionally capped at 10 MB instead of `max_image_size_kb`, preventing sites configured for larger images from importing otherwise-valid image URLs

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows at line 55 that the code changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. This means sites that have configured `max_image_size_kb` to values larger than 10MB (10240 KB) will now be unable to import images via API URL that exceed 10MB, even though their configuration should allow it. This is a real behavioral change that breaks expected functionality for sites with larger image size limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated-image handling uses the extensionless temporary-file path instead of the original filename, bypassing `_animated` processing and potentially flattening oversized animated GIFs

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In uploads_controller.rb line 67, the code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. The `tempfile.path` is an extensionless temporary file path, but the `optimize` method in optimized_image.rb checks `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` to determine if animated processing should be used. Since the tempfile path won't have a .GIF extension, animated GIFs will be processed with non-animated instructions, potentially flattening them to static images.
